messages:
support_lynn: Heads-up — customer MapleAI opened a high-priority ticket: their embedding vector size dropped after we pinned a model. Previously 1536, now 1024, causing their indexer to reject inserts. They started seeing errors right after the model freeze at ~14:20Z. Logs attached in the ticket.

elaine: Can you paste the exact API request + model identifier they used?

support_lynn: "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood/emb-legacy-1536@pin-2026-03-15\",\"input\":\"...batch of 128 strings...\"}'"

frank: Embedding dimension is part of the public contract for that model family — pinning should not change dims. Possible alias/variant substitution?

sanjay: Running a quick repro with their payload now (same batch size). I see the runtime returning vectors of length 1024 when the pinned alias resolves to `embed-lite-q8`. Looks like alias mapping for the pinned identifier pointed at a quantized variant with a different embedding head.

opsbot: Deploy bot: pinned-variant-swap completed — alias redwood/emb-legacy-1536@pin-2026-03-15 -> redwood/embed-lite-q8 (completed at 2026-03-15T14:20:13Z).

jake: That explains it. embed-lite-q8 is a smaller architecture, output dim 1024. Two quick immediate actions: 1) reproduce locally and confirm shape, 2) provide customer mitigation. Repro steps I used: 
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={\"model\":\"redwood/emb-legacy-1536@pin-2026-03-15\",\"input\":[\"a\",\"b\"]}, headers={\"Authorization\":\"Bearer X\"})
print(len(resp.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))
```
Got 1024.

support_lynn: Customer error text: "Indexing failed: shape mismatch expected 1536, got 1024" and they have millions of docs. They asked for a rollback or guaranteed compat.

elaine: Mitigation plan: create a short-term API shim that pads returned embeddings with zeros to 1536 for this pinned model id, mark as temporary, and rollback the pin to the previous artifact while we fix mapping. Need approval for a quick rollback and a hotfix pad route.

frank: Approve rollback. Padding is acceptable as temporary mitigation but we should warn the customer about semantic differences. We'll also need a migration plan for their index to re-ingest with correct vectors later.

sanjay: Performed rollback of the alias to the prior artifact at 14:45Z. Verifying live now — running the same repro shows 1536 vectors again.

opsbot: Deploy bot: alias rollback completed at 2026-03-15T14:45:02Z.

jake: I'll open an internal PR to: 1) add validation during pin/alias operations that asserts output embedding dim matches the pinned model's canonical dim, 2) add a CI check in model onboarding to surface mismatch warnings for quantized variants, 3) add an ops-only flag to allow explicit override with confirmation.

elaine: I'll message the customer with status: rollback done, temporary padding available if they want immediate compatibility, we recommend re-ingest when we ship the longer-term fix. They prefer rollback + no-pad; will run sanity checks and report back.

support_lynn: Customer confirmed they see 1536 again and are running ingestion smoke tests. They asked for a postmortem and a timeline for the pinning safety guard.

frank: Root cause summary for the future PM/eng note: pinned alias resolved to a quantized/smaller variant (`embed-lite-q8`) with a different embedding head. Pinning tool allowed mapping across architectures without validating output contract. Action items: validation on pin, better alias transparency in console (show variant dims), and an incident runbook for embedding-dim mismatches (pad-shim, rollback, notify).

jake: PR opened: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 — adds dim-check on pin + webhook alert to support if mismatch detected. Assigning reviewers: @frank @sanjay.

support_lynn: Customer happy for now, will keep the ticket open until ingestion completes. Closing ops note: watch for any other pinned artifacts that may alias to smaller architectures. :white_check_mark:
